contribution.concept: Multi-task character-level attentional network model for medical concept normalization

evidence.evidence: In this work, we present a multi-task character-level attentional network model for medical concept normalization.
Other two real-world English datasets are also used.
In this work, we present a multi-task character-level attentional network model for medical concept normalization.
Specifically, the character-level encoding scheme of our model can alleviate the OOV word problem.
The attention mechanism can effectively exploit the word morphological information through multi-task training.
It generates higher attention weights on domain-related positions in the text sequence, helping the downstream convolution focus on the characters that are related to medical concepts.

problem.concept: Existing word-level methods cannot learn character structure features and suffer from OOV words

evidence.evidence: However, they have two main limitations: (1) Existing word-level methods cannot learn character structure features inside words and suffer from “Out-of-vocabulary” (OOV) words, which are common in noisy colloquial text.
Hence the word morphological information inside the concept is lost.
